schema:name: Russ Kramer and Workers Overlooking Naturally Dried Coffee Beans, Sumatra, Indonesia
schema:description: This image shows Russ Kramer, president of Hacienda La Minita, overlooking coffee beans drying on a patio. This drying method produces what is referred to as "naturally processed" coffee, as opposed to "wet processed" or "washed" coffee. In the natural drying process, the fruit is left intact and spread out on patios or raised beds, then hulled when a certain moisture content level is reached. In contrast, the wet process involves depulping and washing off the residual mucilage before the coffee is dried and further processed. The natural process depends on a particular climate and is less controlled than the wet process. Hacienda La Minita serves as Distant Lands Coffee’s green coffee trading division, sourcing specialty coffee from countries such as Ethiopia. Coffee in Ethiopia is grown largely by smallholder farmers and processed at local cooperatives and washing stations.
